name: Skateboard: push, turn and stop
blurb: Before any tricks: riding comfortably, turning by leaning and stopping on demand. Most people skip these and then wonder why the ollie will not come.
gear: A complete skateboard with soft-ish wheels for learning
Helmet, and wrist guards are genuinely worth it
steps: Find your stance: whichever foot you would naturally lead with. Have someone gently push you from behind to find out.
Practise standing and rolling on grass or carpet first, then on flat smooth ground.
Learn to push properly: front foot over the front bolts pointing forward, push with the back foot, then turn the front foot sideways.
Learn to turn by leaning on your heels and toes rather than by scraping the tail.
Learn to stop three ways: foot braking, riding out onto grass, and stepping off forwards at speed.
Learn to fall: crouch low, roll, and do not put a stiff arm out.
tips: Loosen or tighten your trucks to taste — too tight and it will not turn, too loose and it wobbles at speed.
Learning to fall properly is not optional. Wrist fractures are the most common skate injury by far.
proof: You push, ride 100 metres, turn both ways around obstacles and stop where you intend to.
